question.problem: Estimate the area under the curve $y={x}^{2}-2x+2$ over the interval $[1,3]$ using a left Riemann sum with step size $Δx=0.5.$ Is this an overestimate or an underestimate?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14221930/assets/2cd664908ea218fecf5a33ea3312bd883f5495d64fc0da8387632a7d2e17c26a.png)

The area $A$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(1)+f(1.5)+f(2)+f(2.5)}})\cdot {{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $2.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $1.25$ | $2$ | $3.25$ |

Finally, we obtain the following approximation for our area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(1+1.25+2+3.25)\cdot 0.5 \\  & =7.5\cdot 0.5 \\  & =3.75\end{aligned}
$$

Because the function is *strictly increasing* over the interval $[1,3],$ the rectangles reach *below* the function, which means our approximation is an *underestimate* of the actual area.
